questions.q: Which of these is a reason to drop uninformative features?
options: It guarantees a higher training score
It reduces overfitting risk, training cost, and the number of pipelines that can break
It removes the need for a test set
It makes the target column unnecessary
questions.explain: Fewer irrelevant features means less noise to memorize, cheaper training and serving, and easier explanations. It does not guarantee a higher training score or replace evaluation.

questions.q: SelectKBest with f_regression is an example of which family of methods?
options: Wrapper, because it retrains a model repeatedly
Embedded, because it selects during model training
Filter, because it scores each feature independently with a statistic
Unsupervised, because it ignores the target
questions.explain: SelectKBest ranks each feature by a statistic (here an F-test against the target) without training a model on subsets, which makes it a filter method.

questions.q: Why can RFE choose a different feature set than SelectKBest on the same data?
options: Because RFE ignores the target
Because SelectKBest randomly shuffles features
Because RFE only works on categorical data
Because a wrapper judges features together while a filter scores each one alone
questions.explain: In the lesson, RFE kept s1 and s2, which are strongly related to each other, while the filter kept different columns. Wrappers evaluate combinations; filters do not.

questions.q: What is the safest way to do feature selection when cross-validating?
options: Select features on the full dataset first, then cross-validate
Choose the features that score best on the test set
Put the selector in a pipeline so it is refit on each training fold
Select features once by hand and never re-check them
questions.explain: Selecting on all rows lets information from validation rows influence which features are kept. A pipeline refits the selector using only each fold's training data.

questions.q: In the lesson, four selected features scored a mean R² of 0.460 versus 0.482 for all ten. What is the fair conclusion?
options: Four features recovered most of the performance with a simpler model, but the trade should be judged case by case
Selection always improves accuracy
Selection always hurts accuracy
The difference proves the model was leaking
questions.explain: The simpler model lost only a little performance. Whether that trade is worth it depends on your goals, so measure it rather than assume a universal rule.
